description: Solo dev from Thailand (SYDEAR). Project: Field Shift — a tool helping Thai farmers adapt planting calendars with NASA POWER rainfall and temperature data. 5 years of Phitsanulok data shows rain varies hugely year to year, so fixed calendars fail. Looking for teammates with farming/agriculture knowledge or data visualization skills. Thai speakers welcome. My skills: software, data, AI.
summary: FieldShift is a mobile-first, zero-backend crop-rotation decision-support web app built for smallholder rice farmers in Chai Nam, Wang Thong, Phitsanulok, Thailand (16.845925N, 100.466731E). Using 25 years of NASA POWER climatology (2001-2025), 2024 daily weather, ISRIC SoilGrids data, and verified Thai agricultural benchmarks, FieldShift helps farmers compare dry-season options after rice (Fallow vs. Chai Nat 84-1 Mungbean vs. Sunn Hemp cover crop) based on their own priorities - water scarcity, income, soil recovery, yield, or risk - without claiming to forecast future weather.
details: Rice farmers in Chai Nam, Wang Thong, Phitsanulok, Thailand face an uncertain dry season (Nov-Apr): only 28.8 mm of rain fell Nov-Feb 2024, and April-May heat reached 42.9 C. After the main rice harvest, should they leave the field fallow, or plant a dry-season crop? FieldShift is a mobile-first, zero-backend web app (static HTML/CSS/JS on GitHub Pages) that compares three strategies from historical NASA POWER and ISRIC SoilGrids data - NOT a weather forecast. A: Rice only (current, fallow in the dry season). B: Rice + Mungbean Chai Nat 84-1 (65 days, about 153 kg/rai farmer yield, needs irrigation 2-3 times). C: Rice + Sunn Hemp green manure (50-60 days, 1.5-3.0 t/rai biomass, about 10-20 kg N/rai, rebuilds soil). Rice stays the main crop in all three strategies. Farmers set their own priorities with 5 sliders (yield, water use, extra income, soil health, risk) or tap a quick scenario preset, and the ranking updates instantly with plain-language reasons - including a 'What if I change my mind?' sensitivity mode that shows how #1 flips. All climate and soil values come directly from embedded NASA POWER and SoilGrids JSON files; every crop benchmark cites Thai DOA / LDD / OAE and international sources (see SOURCES.md in the repo). Historical comparison only - never a yield guarantee; the farmer makes the final decision. NASA Data: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER API (PRECTOTCORR, T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, WS2M - both 2001-2025 monthly climatology v2.10.1 and full 2024 daily series v2.10.3 at grid 16.846N, 100.467E), combined with ISRIC SoilGrids v2 (clay, silt, sand, phh2o, soc at 0-5 cm and 5-15 cm). Use of Super Intelligence (AI disclosure): AI assistance (Antigravity / Gemini) was used to cross-reference Thai Department of Agriculture (DOA), Land Development Department (LDD), and Office of Agricultural Economics (OAE) crop benchmarks (CROPS.md), structure the offline-capable static UI (docs/), write automated dataset parity checks (scripts/verify_data.mjs), and prepare bilingual Thai/English copy. All climate and soil values in the application come directly from the embedded NASA POWER and SoilGrids JSON files and verified institutional sources.
